changes: Carlo Acutis banner overlay: strips a leading "Miracle of " from the entry name before display
(new carloDisplayName() helper) — matches the real exhibition site's own red-band style, which
shows just the place ("GERONA") beneath a separate "Eucharistic Miracle of" script line already
in the banner artwork, rather than repeating "Miracle of" twice. Only strips that exact leading
phrase; names that don't start with it (e.g. "First Miracle of Turin", "Rosano") are untouched.
Also switched the overlay font from Cinzel to a plain bold serif (Georgia/Times) with tighter
letter-spacing, closer to the exhibition site's own typography.
Fix: the Carlo Acutis banner's name overlay (added in v148) rendered invisibly on real Safari —
the button's height was only ever established by its content (the image), so the absolutely
positioned name box's percentage top/height had no definite containing-block height to resolve
against and ended up laid out outside the button's visible, overflow:hidden area. Fixed with the
classic percentage-padding trick (.carloLinkBtn::before with padding-top matching the banner's
own 900:336 ratio) to give the button a genuinely definite pixel height, and the image is now
absolutely positioned to fill it (object-fit:cover) instead of defining it. Also dropped the cqw
container-query font sizing in favor of the site's existing calc(px * var(--txt)) convention,
removing a second dependency on newer CSS support. No HTML/data changes — CSS-only fix.
Carlo Acutis section now shows the exhibition's own banner artwork (Images/CarloAcutis/banner.jpg
— the "Eucharistic Miracle" photo/gold-script/red-band header from miracolieucaristici.org) with
rounded corners as a tappable button, in place of the earlier plain icon+text row. Tapping it opens
that entry's own carloLinks.url. Upload the image to Images/CarloAcutis/banner.jpg in the repo —
same one asset reused across every "found" Eucharistic Miracle entry, not per-entry.
New Carlo Acutis Links table (db.carloLinks), separate from an entry's regular art.links.
Eucharistic Miracle entries no longer carry their miracolieucaristici.org link inside
"Sources & Further Reading" — it now gets its own dedicated section on the article, styled
distinctly (violet accent, host-and-chalice icon) with a "See Carlo's Work" link, echoing the
exhibition's own site. Each row is {id, entityId, kind:"carloLink", status:"found"|"pending",
url, note}. status:"found" renders the section; status:"pending" (or a missing row entirely)
renders nothing to visitors, but shows the research note in an amber box when Review Mode is
on, so the gap is visible to the owner without leaking an unfinished state publicly.
Paste JSON now also accepts {"carloLinks":[...], "carloLinkDeletions":[...]}, alongside or
instead of entries/deletions in the same paste. New Export tab button, "JSON — Carlo Links",
dumps the whole table for review (which ones are still "pending" is visible directly from the
export — no separate tracking field needed).
Review Mode banner on the timeline now just says "Review Mode" and carries a "Show Only
Pending" button that narrows the whole canvas down to held-for-review entries only (ignoring
the category/region chips), so they're all visible at a glance instead of scattered among
everything else. Toggling Review Mode off always clears this back to the normal full view.
Export tab (Manage → Export) has a new "Held for Review Only" filter chip alongside category/
region/years, applied consistently across JSON — Filtered, Excel, and CSV-fallback export.
Review Mode now has a direct switch in the hamburger settings menu, right next to Owner
Tools, showing the pending count right on the row — no more having to remember that it only
lived inside Manage → Entries. Both switches (hamburger and the one still in Manage) share
one setReviewMode() setter so flipping either always keeps the other in sync.
Hero clock frames moved from Images/heroClock/heroClock_NNN.jpg to a flat
Images/heroClock_NNN.jpg — GitHub's mobile web uploader has no folder-creation control, so a
subfolder meant either a tedious per-file path edit or a device-level workaround. Flat
filenames mean the 40 frames upload the same way every other image already does: straight
into Images/, no extra step. No behavior change, path-only.
Header hero graphic replaced: the static dome-and-cross image is out, and #heroLogo is now a
40-frame clock animation (Images/heroClock/heroClock_001.jpg … 040.jpg, preloaded on load).
It no longer plays on a timer — it's scrubbed directly by horizontal timeline scrolling:
dragging/scrolling the timeline left (moving forward through history) steps the clock's hands
forward frame by frame; scrolling right (moving backward through history) steps them
backward. Driven by scrollLeft delta on #viewport, throttled through requestAnimationFrame
the same way scheduleBandIconFade already is, so it costs at most one extra img.src swap per
frame. Clamped (not looped) at both ends, since the first and last source frames don't share
a hand position — continuing to scroll past either end just holds on that end frame rather
than jump-cutting. All existing #heroLogo CSS (size, mask, opacity fade, breakpoint) is
untouched; only the element's src now changes instead of staying fixed.
Timeline focus glow reworked: selecting a new entry (tap on the timeline, a search result,
today's feast, or closing an article) now always centers on it and makes it the one pulsing
glow, while whatever was previously the pulsing focus steps down to a steady (non-pulsing,
dimmer) glow instead of continuing to pulse alongside the new one. Only ever one entry pulses
and one shows the steady "you were just here" glow at a time.
Tapping any entry icon directly on the timeline now also centers the view on it (as close as
the scroll range allows) before opening its preview card, instead of just opening the card in
place — matters most for icons near a screen edge, but applied uniformly for consistency.
Added shared setTimelineFocus()/centerAndFocus() helpers so this bookkeeping is consistent
everywhere an entry gets focused, rather than four separate copies of the same logic.
iPhone install instructions: dropped "the" from steps 1 and 2; step 3 now reads "Press [+]
Add to Home Screen after [chevron] View More (bottom)" (was "under the ... (bottom right)") —
shorter, and now wraps to two lines instead of three.
Icon jitter, round 2 (diagnosed from a second screen recording): moving the icon's position to
JS (done in v137/v140 to fix the touching-the-next-band bug) traded one problem for another —
JS position only updates on 'scroll' events, which iOS coalesces to well under 60fps during a
fast fling, so the icon visibly stepped/lagged behind the smoothly-scrolling page around it.
Position is back to native CSS position:sticky (compositor-driven, perfectly smooth, matches
the label exactly) now that v140 already removed the real cause of the old touching bug (the
resize-triggered full re-render, not sticky itself). Opacity alone stays JS-driven for the
fade-before-touching behavior — a little lag there reads as a soft cross-fade, not a stutter.
Found the actual cause of the "too much coffee" jittery/flickering band icons (diagnosed from
a screen recording, frame-by-frame): an existing window 'resize' handler ran a full render()
(wipes and rebuilds the entire canvas) on every resize event, and iOS Safari fires 'resize'
repeatedly during ordinary scrolling as its address-bar toolbar shows/hides — not just on real
rotations. That caused the whole timeline, icons included, to briefly blank out and rebuild
mid-scroll. The resize handler is now debounced (220ms) so rapid-fire scroll-driven resizes
collapse into a single render once things settle; real resizes/rotations still work.
Also dropped the CSS opacity transition on the band icon — it was fighting the JS-driven
per-scroll-frame opacity updates (chasing a constantly-moving target), adding a second,
smaller layer of jitter on top of the render flash. Opacity now just tracks scroll directly.
Band icon positioning/fade rewritten to be fully JS-computed on scroll instead of relying on
CSS position:sticky with combined top+bottom offsets, which behaved inconsistently inside a
manually-scrolled container on mobile Safari — this was the source of the occasional "weird"
fade behavior (icon not fading, or fading unpredictably) some entries showed.
Icon now fades to exactly 0% opacity the instant it would touch/overlap the band below it
(previously bottomed out around 5-10%, never fully gone).
Icon's vertical slot is now clamped the same way for every band (fixed gap below the label,
fixed floor above the band's own bottom edge), so the consistent padding that only the first
band used to get is now guaranteed for all of them.
iPhone install instructions step 1 shortened to "Press the [dots icon] (bottom right)" —
dropped "circle with three dots" now that the icon itself is drawn inline, so the step fits
on one line instead of wrapping.
Replaced the v134 horizontal (entry-proximity) icon fade entirely — the band icon no longer
reacts to entries/icons scrolling by on the timeline at all.
New vertical fade: the band icon now stays at full opacity until its own band's bottom edge
(i.e. the next category's band) is about to scroll up and touch/overlap it, at which point it
fades down; it fades back to full opacity once there's clearance again.
Label text nudged back up to 14px (was 13px).
Icon now sits with a guaranteed padding gap below the label bar (top offset 106 -> 102,
tuned against the smaller label height so the gap stays consistent) so it never touches the
band/label above it.
Icon now casts a visible drop shadow beneath it.
Band icon is now fully opaque at rest (solid two-tone background, no see-through to the
band or entries behind it).
Band icon now fades toward the leftmost visible entry in its own lane as you scroll right,
so the icon and an approaching entry row no longer sit visibly on top of each other; fades
back to full opacity once that entry scrolls away again.
Band label text sized down a notch (16px -> 13px) and the label bar made a touch thinner,
per feedback that it read too large.
Icon now sits a little lower below the label (top offset 96 -> 106) and is bottom-constrained
within its own band, so a band's icon no longer pokes up and tucks under the next band's
label as it scrolls out of view.
Reworked the v132 band-label icon: it's no longer inside the fading label bar (which was
blocking the in-band century numbers as it scrolled right). The label bar is back to
text-only, sticky left, fading out to the right exactly as before.
The category icon is now its own sticky-left element, stuck just below the label, in a
larger framed box (56x56) with its own background — sized and positioned like a small
mosaic/artwork tile rather than a small glyph.
Added TYPE_BAND_IMG (near the ICONS constant) so hosted artwork/mosaic images can be
dropped in per category later — falls back to the existing SVG glyph when empty.
Category band labels (SAINTS, COUNCILS, PERSECUTIONS, MARIAN, EUCHARISTIC, EVENTS) are now
bigger and bolder, with the category's icon displayed underneath the label text.
Folded Manual Cross-Links into the one existing Paste JSON box instead of a separate box —
it now detects a curated link list (lines that aren't valid JSON but each carry the required
two "::" separators) and applies it the same way, same Apply button. One box for entries,
deletions, and links, matching how Tom actually wants to paste things.
New: Manual Cross-Links tool in Manage → Export tab, right under Auto-Link Cross-References.
For curated links the name-matcher can't make safely — a different name for the same person
("Saul" -> St. Paul), a title instead of a name ("the beloved disciple" -> St. John), or a
bare "Mary" meant specifically as the Blessed Virgin. Format: one link per line, entryId ::
exact text :: targetId, with an optional 4th field to pick which occurrence of that text
(default: first). Reuses the same tag-aware scanning as Auto-Link so it never breaks existing
HTML or double-links inside an anchor that's already there. Preview/Apply, same pattern as
Auto-Link. Built so link instructions can be handed over as a short list instead of re-pasting
full article bodies for every cross-link.
iPhone instructions now 5 steps instead of 4, matching the real share-sheet flow: 1) press
the three-dot circle, 2) press Share, 3) find "Add to Home Screen", 4) try View More (bottom
right) if it isn't there, 5) press Add.
View More icon corrected — it's a soft circle with a downward chevron, not three dots (Tom
sent a screenshot of the actual glyph).
Install-instructions row no longer shows two headings. The row's own label now becomes
"iPhone App Instructions" / "Android Instructions" / "Install Instructions" when expanded,
and reverts to "Make this into an App" when collapsed — the separate title line under it is
gone.
iPhone step 3 shortened to "Press View More ⋯" (dropped the trailing "(bottom right)") so it
fits on one line instead of wrapping.
Settings panel top offset nudged up (58px → 46px) now that removing the duplicate heading
frees a bit more vertical room.
Added dedicated Android manual-install instructions (three-dot overflow menu → Add to Home
screen/Install app → Add/Install), shown when a phone is detected as Android and the browser
didn't offer a one-tap beforeinstallprompt (e.g. Firefox or Samsung Internet). Chrome/Edge on
Android still get the genuine one-tap install button as before — this is only the fallback
path, styled to match the iPhone instructions (bold key words, drawn icons).
New: Feast of the Day welcome. On launch (when not opening a shared/deep link), the app
looks up today's date against each saint's "Feast day" fact, and if one matches, travels
there — starting from the usual overview, pausing briefly, then flying to the saint slowly
and deliberately (about 2.4x a normal search jump) before popping open their detail card.
Picks the most prominent (lowest-tier) saint if more than one shares the day. Silently does
nothing if no saint's feast falls on today or if facts/Feast day data is missing/unparsable.
Apostolic Age's 25/50/75 tick labels now match the full century-mark styling (bright gold,
13px) instead of the dimmer/smaller "minor" tick style — they were being treated as lesser
ticks even though they're this zoomed-in era's equivalent of a century mark.
Era band font size up another notch (11.5px → 12.5px), letter-spacing eased slightly further.
Closing an article now leaves a clue on the timeline: the icon you were just reading lights up
(the same gold glow search uses for a match) and the timeline recentres on it, instead of
dropping you back with no trace of where you'd been.
Left/right swipe between chronological neighbors now shares the same back-stack as following
an in-article link — Back can undo a swipe too, landing you back at the same scroll position.
A swipe that lands exactly back where a previous swipe came from pops that frame instead of
pushing a new one, so casual back-and-forth swiping doesn't grow the stack without bound.
Era band font size up a notch (10.5px → 11.5px), letter-spacing eased slightly to compensate.
Hamburger menu reordered: "Make this into an App" (with its expand-to-see install steps) now
sits first, above Font Size — previously it was lower in the list. Combined with the panel
moving higher (top offset 84px → 58px, more usable height), those steps now sit near the top
of the screen instead of getting hidden behind iOS's own share sheet when you actually follow
them.
Added a 4th install step: "Press the circle in the bottom right," after Tom found the
3-step version left one step out on his device.
New: update-available glow. The hamburger pulses gold a few times, once, the first time a
newer version is detected — queued for the moment the panel is next closed, since the icon is
hidden while the panel is open. The "New Version Available" row itself gets the same brief
glow the next time the panel is opened. Neither glows continuously; each fires once per newly
seen version.
Added "Test Update Glow" under Owner Tools — previews both glows on demand (fake "vTEST"
label, auto-reverts after 16s) without needing an actual version mismatch to test against.
Era band (the "Apostolic Age" / "Age of Martyrs" row) redone as one continuous gold
surface — a top-to-bottom highlight/shadow gradient that looks like a single curved
gold bar running the whole width, rather than each era being its own alternating gold
tint. Text is now bold dark navy for contrast. A dark divider line (not a color change)
now marks where one era ends and the next begins.
heroLogo nudged right (right:30px, was 46px) — it was overlapping the "v120" version stamp next to the title on a live screenshot.

heroLogo's fade reworked again: it's now driven directly by how close the article's flying photo actually is to heroLogo's own corner — 0 while it's elsewhere (peek, top of a freshly-opened article, closed), fading toward fully hidden only as the scroll-driven corner badge settles into that exact spot, and back the moment it leaves (article closes, collapses to peek, or the reader scrolls back up). The previous version faded it for a fixed ~220ms window and then always brought it back regardless of whether the badge was still sitting there — this fixes that: as long as the badge occupies the corner, the graphic now stays faded, with no timer to time out.
The fade transition slowed from .3s to 1.2s so it reads as a gradual dissolve rather than a noticeable pop, in both directions.

heroLogo image regenerated without the central-width crop that was cutting off both flanking cupolas — only the dead space above the cross is trimmed now, so the full dome (both side towers included) is visible, matching the owner's reference goal image.
Resized to 150×130px (was 56×74px) to suit the now-wider, uncropped aspect ratio, with the small-screen breakpoint scaled proportionally.

heroLogo shrunk to fit entirely within the header (56×74px, was 122×160px) — it was spilling past the header into the era-band row and crowding the "Age of Martyrs" label on a live screenshot. No new cropping of the source image; this is a pure CSS resize.

heroLogo's fade behavior reworked per owner feedback: it no longer fades just because a peek card or full article is open. It now only fades while the article's flying photo is actually moving through #heroLogo's own top-right corner — the scroll-driven shrink into the corner badge, and the collapse-to-peek flight (not the expand-away-from-the-corner flight, which is leaving that spot, not crossing it). A short idle debounce (220ms) brings it back once the photo has settled rather than the instant a single animation frame ends.
Header graphic replaced with a new dome-and-cross image, re-cropped to trim the dead space above the cross so it sits closer to the image's own top edge.

heroLogo repositioned: shifted up (top:-8px) and further left (right:44px, was right:8px) to give the hamburger menu clear breathing room, per the live-screenshot check showing the two crowding each other.

Header's top background color changed from #0A1430 to #030B20 — sampled directly from the new image's own corner/edge pixels — so the graphic's rectangular edge blends into the page instead of showing a visible seam.
Timeline search box narrowed from 320px to 224px (about 70% of its former width) and its text enlarged, staying above the 16px floor that keeps iOS Safari from auto-zooming on focus.

New fixed header graphic (Images/heroLogo.png, a cropped dome-and-cross image) fills the gap the narrower search box opened up next to the hamburger menu, reaching from the top of the screen down through the header and controls bar to the edge of the timeline. Edges are softened with a CSS mask rather than a hard rectangle. It is decorative and non-interactive (pointer-events:none) so it never blocks taps on the hamburger, search box, or timeline pins.
The graphic fades out via body.artOpen whenever a card (peek) or full article opens, so it never competes with open content — the same convention the earlier, since-removed monstrance graphic used.

Wired up the true installable-PWA icon path that was already scaffolded in the file: the APP_ICON constant now points at real hosted icon files (Images/icons/apple-touch-icon.png, icon-192.png, icon-512.png) instead of null, so Add to Home Screen picks up the new gold-domed cross artwork instead of the old embedded placeholder.
Runtime web manifest's background_color changed to a gold/cream tone to match the new icon's launch/splash feel; theme_color and app name unchanged.
No changes to the timeline, article view, or Content Manager in this build.

Content Manager fully reskinned to match the app's own Settings sheet throughout, not just the Logs tab: sans-serif system font, larger text, and flat white rows on a light gray page background in place of the gold-tinted, Cinzel/EB Garamond serif card look used everywhere else in the CMS (Entries, Export, Import, Settings, the exit-confirmation dialog).

The tab menu moved from a scrolling row under the header to a fixed bottom tab bar — icon over label, five equal-width thumb-reachable targets, matching standard iOS tab-bar placement. The Content Manager top bar now holds only the title and Exit.
The public-facing timeline and article view are untouched — this redesign is scoped entirely to the owner-only Content Manager chrome.
Logs tab: dates now display as "Monday 8/8  12:45 PM" instead of the raw ISO timestamp.

The button beside search now reads "Search" and explicitly re-runs the filter, instead of "Refresh" (data still reloads automatically every time the Logs tab is opened, so nothing was lost by dropping the separate refresh action).
Search matches are now highlighted in yellow across version, date, and change text.

Redesigned the Logs tab to mimic the app's own Settings sheet rather than the rest of the Content Manager's serif/gold theme: sans-serif system font throughout, larger text, and flat full-height rows in place of the small boxed card. Change lists are now numbered (1, 2, 3…) instead of bulleted. The panel now cancels the surrounding padding so it runs edge-to-edge and fills the remaining screen height.

Replaced the header's gear/hamburger icon (was the ⚙/☰ unicode characters, which iOS renders as a glossy 3D emoji-style glyph) with a flat, simple, single-color SVG gear/lines icon that follows the site's gold color exactly.

Fixed the gear icon overlapping the Content Manager's Exit button: the gear sits at a fixed top-right position with a high z-index (so it stays reachable from any screen, including Manage), which the new sticky Content Manager header didn't leave room for. The header now reserves space on the right for it, and Exit is wider with more breathing room.

Content Manager header simplified: Exit button now just reads "Exit" instead of "Exit Content Manager", and the version badge now matches the "Content Manager" title's font (Cinzel) instead of a different serif.
